title: CCC 2026 — School & Data/AI
summary: Placed 14th in School and 31st in Data/AI with team PretrainedLanguageModel in an intense edition marked by matchmaking bottlenecks and AI subscription vibecoders.
body: CCC 2026 was a very interesting experience, even though this year we didn't manage to achieve our best results — finishing 31st in Data/AI with team PretrainedLanguageModel and 14th in the School category.

In the Data/AI track, our progress was heavily impacted by what our team felt was a poorly designed matchmaking system. Because the queue rarely placed us into matches, we were unable to play nearly enough games with our AI — ending up with around 100 matches while other teams had 300–400 matches, and at times waiting 10 minutes without getting into a single match.

Combined with competitors using paid AI subscriptions ('vibecoders') to generate solutions faster without explicit prompting, we watched our ranking drop from 2nd down to 10th, 20th, and 31st toward the end as we sat out of matchmaking. A similar dynamic with paid AI subscriptions affected the School category as well, where we finished in 14th place.

title: ROSDC 2026
summary: Worked on the Operations department in the Romanian Space Design Competition under fictional aerospace company Condor, collaborating with creative students on a complex aerospace engineering proposal.

links.label: Instagram (@ro.sdc)
links.description: Official Instagram page of the Romanian Space Design Competition (ROSDC).

body: ROSDC 2026 (Romanian Space Design Competition) was a wonderful experience! Held as an industry-style aerospace engineering and space settlement design simulation, the competition brings high school students together into fictional aerospace companies — such as Condor — to respond to a complex Request for Proposal (RFP) for future space habitats and orbital infrastructure.
I worked on the Operations side of the project, focusing on how the settlement and systems actually function, scale, and sustain daily life and logistics in space.

Beyond the engineering challenge itself, the best part of ROSDC 2026 was meeting so many creative people with truly awesome ideas and collaborating under pressure to turn ambitious concepts into a cohesive design pitch.

title: From Algorithms to Neurons
summary: 1st place in the AI Competition (Group A) and 9th place in the 24h Hackathon at Constanța Maritime University.
body: From Algorithms to Neurons was a five-day AI, STEM, signal processing and technology event in Constanța, organized with IEEE Romania Section and Informatică pentru Viitor.
I placed 1st in the AI Competition (Group A, Grades 7–10) with ~260/300 points focusing on Signal Analysis and audio processing, and achieved 9th place in the 24-hour hackathon with team Camera 505.

title: RISE Final Round
summary: Second place at the RISE Final Round after a stronger final with harder AI tasks.
body: RISE was one of the competition results that gave me a lot of confidence. The final round was harder than the qualifier and forced me to stay calm while solving AI-style tasks under pressure.
This work entry is here because I want the Work section to track outcomes and the process behind them, not only the final placement.

title: Skillab Innovation Challenge
summary: First place with a project around skills, labour-market analytics, and AI-assisted insight.
body: Skillab was the hackathon connected to Cluj IT Cluster where my team built Skillab Radar, a project around skills, labour-market analytics, and AI-assisted insight.
The challenge was more product-oriented than most contests I join. We had to connect AI, data, and a useful idea in a way that made sense outside a pure coding contest.
The repo is linked here because this is one of the projects where the implementation matters as much as the presentation.

title: NitroNLP Hackathon
summary: Third place with PretrainedLanguageModel in a fast NLP hackathon on Nitro-AI Judge.
body: NitroNLP was a fast team-based NLP competition. It rewarded quick iteration, practical evaluation, and communication inside the team.
This belongs in Work because it was a concrete applied NLP build under contest constraints.

title: ROAI Selection Camp Qualifier
summary: A high-pressure qualifier round that pushed my practical ML and contest strategy.
body: The ROAI Selection Camp Qualifier was useful because it exposed weaknesses in how I manage experiments and time. It was not only about knowing ML, but also about choosing the right experiment quickly.
I keep this in Work because it shaped how I think about AI competitions: practical decisions matter as much as the model itself.

title: CCC School & Data/AI
summary: Placed 4th in School and 12th in Data/AI, mixing algorithmic speed with data thinking.
body: CCC mixed level-based programming with data and AI thinking. I liked it because the structure rewarded persistence: each improvement unlocked more of the task.
It is a good example of the kind of work I enjoy most: problem solving that sits somewhere between algorithms, data, and practical implementation.
